Subject: NUS News: 24 Sep – 5 Oct 2026
Preview: 24 Sep – 5 Oct 2026 NUS reaches highest-ever position at 15th in THE World University Rankings 2027 NUS has risen to 15th place globally in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings 2027 — its highest-ever position since the rankings were established. It remains at 3rd in Asia and 1st in Singapore. The University’s rise this year was driven largely by stronger scores in teaching and research, with deliberate efforts over the years to strengthen the quality of its education, raise the rigour and relevance of its research, and deepen its partnerships across the world. Read more NUS Chairman Hsieh Fu Hua hands over the helm to Leo Yip after a decade of transformation Mr Hsieh Fu Hua will be stepping down after a decade as Chairman of NUS’ Board of Trustees (BOT) on 31 March 2027, and will be succeeded by former Head of Civil Service Mr Leo Yip on 1 April. Under Mr Hsieh’s stewardship, NUS significantly expanded interdisciplinary education and launched numerous initiatives to develop future-ready graduates, enhance research impact and deepen partnerships with industry and community. His successor Mr Yip, Deputy Chairman of the BOT, brings to the role more than four decades of distinguished public service and leadership. Read more NUS team unveils electronic skin that lets users “see” touch instantly NUS researchers have developed the eLuminator, a next-generation electronic skin that can sense and directly visualise pressure in real time, led by Professor Lim Chwee Teck from the NUS Department of Biomedical Engineering and the Institute for Health Innovation & Technology (iHealthtech). Addressing key limitations of current wearable sensing technologies, the team’s soft, ultrathin device enables a more responsive human-machine interface and easier integration into wearable and biomedical technologies. Read more NParks and NUS launch S$60M National Institute for Marine and Ocean Sciences to strengthen Singapore’s coastal resilience NParks and NUS launched the National Institute for Marine and Ocean Sciences (NIMOS) on 22 Sep 2026, a national research institute to strengthen Singapore’s capabilities in protecting its marine environment and sustainably managing its coastal and marine spaces. Taking a whole-of-coast approach, NIMOS will develop targeted management and conservation strategies; advance Singapore’s blue economy; build local talent and capabilities; and establish Singapore as a regional thought leader in marine science. Read more NUS Geography offers a front-row seat to a world reshaped by climate change, AI and rapid urban transformation NUS Geography has ranked first in the 2026 ShanghaiRanking Global Ranking of Academic Subjects and 4th in the 2026 QS World University Rankings by Subject — a testament to the Department’s academic and research prowess. Over the years, it has expanded its teaching and research to address a changing world shaped by complex issues like climate change, AI, sustainability and rapid urban transformation — expanding the boundaries of geographic inquiry to uncover new questions and possibilities about the places we inhabit. Read more Beyond the safari: CAPT students uncover lessons in conservation and community in Botswana Over two weeks in Botswana, 24 NUS College of Alice & Peter Tan (CAPT) students learnt what conservation looks like on the ground — visiting the wetlands of the Okavango Delta and hearing from community groups and conservation practitioners on the everyday negotiations between humans and wildlife. Their visit was part of the Study Trips for Engagement and EnRichment (STEER) programme, which gives students first-hand exposure to the diverse sociocultural environments of emerging regions. Read more NUS SCALE Dean Chai Kah Hin on making learning a habit for life As the NUS School of Continuing and Lifelong Education (SCALE) marks its 10th anniversary, its Dean, Associate Professor Chai Kah Hin, reflects on how AI, changing careers and longer lives are reshaping education. He envisages a university that people can continually return to throughout their lives, where learning is not an occasional response to disruption, but an integral part of everyday life — in the true spirit of lifelong education. Read more NUS, Applied Materials and Micron join forces to grow Singapore’s next-generation semiconductor talent NUS signed an MOU with industry leaders Applied Materials and Micron on 23 Sep 2026 to strengthen the pipeline of industry-ready talent for Singapore’s expanding semiconductor sector at the Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association Summit. Under the agreement, outstanding students pursuing the NUS Master of Science in Semiconductor Technology & Operations programme will be considered for scholarships and internships with the two companies, as well as employment opportunities upon graduation. Since its inception in 2001, it has grown from a humble research institute into a global hub for Asia-centred research, spanning six research clusters, four strategic programmes, and international partnerships from Kazakhstan to South Korea. To date, it has undertaken over 117 unique projects delivering impact in areas including environmental planning amid climate change and effective eldercare for ageing populations. Subject: [For all Postgraduates] Register for our upcoming Career Booster workshops in Sept & Oct!
Preview: Dear students Thank you for your enthusiastic response to our Career Booster workshops so far! As we move into the middle of the semester, please refer to the remaining workshops scheduled in Sept and Oct 2026 . All workshops will be conducted either virtually via Zoom (you will receive details upon successful registration) or physically at the YIH03-05 CareerSpace ( directions ). Date/Time Workshop Description 16 Sep (Wed) 10am-12pm Inside Fintech Hiring: Roles, Skills & Market Signals Curious about what it takes to break into fintech? Join hiring leaders from Aspire, and KPay for an insider's look at the fintech talent market and what employers seek in the next generation of talent. The panel discussion will explore the diverse roles driving growth across the fintech sector, the technical and transferable skills that stand out during recruitment, and practical strategies for succeeding in internship and graduate hiring processes. Speakers will also share their perspectives on emerging industry trends, from artificial intelligence and digital payments to evolving customer expectations, and how these developments are creating new opportunities across the sector. Whether you are interested in product management, software engineering, data and analytics, operations, business development, risk, compliance, or other functions, this session will provide valuable insights to help you better understand the fintech ecosystem and position yourself for success. 17 Sep (Thu) 2-5pm Think Like a Consultant: Case Study Simulation Workshop What does it take to solve a real-world business problem under time pressure? In this immersive, hands-on workshop by Accenture, you will experience a consulting challenge inspired by real assessment and project scenarios used within the industry. Working in teams, participants will tackle an AI-driven business case that mirrors the complexity, ambiguity, and fast-paced nature of consulting engagements. Guided through a structured problem-solving process, you will learn how to analyse challenges, develop practical solutions, and communicate recommendations effectively while adapting to new information and evolving client needs along the way. By participating, you will: - Experience how consultants approach real-world business challenges from problem definition to client presentation - Develop critical thinking, analytical reasoning, and structured communication skills - Gain hands-on experience using AI prompting as a professional problem-solving tool - Understand how consulting firms assess talent and what recruiters look for in candidates - Learn more about career pathways in consulting, strategy, and technology - Connect with industry professionals and gain insights into the consulting profession 21 Sep (Mon) 2-5pm Harnessing Strengths for Workplace Success While we are often told to work on our weaknesses, research shows that leveraging our strengths leads to greater performance, confidence, and well-being. This workshop helps you understand how your strengths show up in daily life and how to harness them during internships and in the workplace. Workshop Activities Will Help You: - Use your strengths to evaluate job fit and work environments. - Build your personal brand on LinkedIn and in interviews. - Apply your strengths to workplace scenarios to enhance effectiveness and collaboration. - Begin your strengths journey and discover how to thrive by doing what you do best. Compulsory Requirements: After registering on NUS TalentConnect, you must complete the Teams Form, including up to three reasons/motivations for taking the CliftonStrengths assessment and joining the workshop. Selection (in oversubscribed cases) will be based on these responses. Pre-Work: All participants must complete the CliftonStrengths Assessment (fully subsidised; usual price S$30). A personalised strengths report will be emailed to you once registered. Please read your report and bring it to the workshop. 25 Sep (Fri) 2-6pm Ace Your Assessment Centre (Postgraduate) Aspiring to join a leading multinational company on a fast-track management programme? Gain an edge through this four-hour intensive training designed to help you excel at assessment centres that is widely used by top employers not only for Management Associate recruitment but also for internal promotions. Led by Geoff Barwise, who has designed assessment centres for leading MNCs, this workshop places you in group-based mock business cases that mirror real-world organisational challenges. Students will navigate group dynamics, work under time pressure, handle challenging interactions, and alternate between participant and observer roles to gain deeper insight into how candidates are evaluated. Key Takeaways: - Build agility and quick thinking to manage uncertainty during assessment exercises. - Practise responding to real scenarios such as business cases, group discussions, and presentations. - Develop essential skills such as diplomatic communication, influencing in teams, and leading difficult conversations. - Receive personalised feedback from expert trainers. 7 Oct (Wed) 2-4pm Navigating Workplace Culture & Diversity Today’s workplaces are increasingly diverse, bringing together individuals with different cultural backgrounds, identities, perspectives, and communication styles. The ability to work effectively across differences is a key professional skill that enables stronger collaboration, innovation, and workplace success. This interactive workshop will help participants develop the awareness, mindset, and practical skills needed to navigate diverse work environments with confidence and professionalism. Through discussions, real-world scenarios, and practical exercises, students will gain a deeper understanding of how culture and diversity influence workplace interactions and learn strategies for fostering inclusive and respectful working relationships. By the end of the workshop, participants will be able to: - Recognise how culture, identity, and diversity can shape workplace interactions and expectations - Identify common communication and collaboration challenges that arise in diverse teams - Practise inclusive behaviours that foster trust, teamwork, and a sense of belonging - Navigate misunderstandings and cultural differences with empathy, professionalism, and respect - Build greater cultural awareness and adaptability in multicultural work environments 13 Oct (Tues) 10am-12pm Managing Job Offers and Salary Negotiation Congratulations! You have received an internship or job offer. But what’s next? Beyond celebrating, you will need to evaluate the offer, understand the contract terms, assess your motivators, and decide how to accept or decline professionally. This workshop helps you navigate these decisions with confidence and integrity. Expert trainer Clement Ong will guide you through case studies, breakout discussions, and live feedback sessions to help you handle job offers and salary negotiations effectively. Participants Will Learn: - Identify your motivators and evaluate employment contracts and remuneration packages. - Professionally and ethically manage multiple job offers (Dos and Don’ts). - Apply negotiation strategies and respond confidently to salary-related questions. - Understand key negotiation techniques used in the workplace. - Accept or decline offers gracefully and professionally. - Handle rejections with composure and confidence. 14 Oct (Wed) 3-4.30pm Careers in Corporate Communication and Public Relations How do organisations shape perceptions, build trust, and communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders? If you have ever wondered what it takes to build a successful career in Corporate Communications or Public Relations (PR), this panel discussion offers an opportunity to learn directly from experienced professionals in the field. Join seasoned practitioners from both corporate and agency settings as they share their career journeys, discuss the realities of working in communications and PR, and provide insights into the skills and attributes needed to thrive in this fast-paced and dynamic industry. The discussion will also explore common career pathways, including the differences between agency and in-house roles, helping students better understand the opportunities available across the profession. Whether you are considering a future in communications, storytelling, media relations, stakeholder engagement, or reputation management, this session will provide valuable perspectives to help you navigate the field with greater clarity and confidence. 16 Oct (Fri) 12-1.30pm Navigating your Job Search: Staying Resilient through Mindfulness Could this be you? The excitement of graduation fades… and the uncertainty begins to creep in. “Will I get a job?” “Why am I facing so many rejections?” You’re not alone. The job search can be stressful, discouraging, and emotionally draining especially when the outcomes don’t match your expectations. Many fresh graduates find themselves in this very place. The good news? You don’t have to stay there. When the going gets tough, the tough get going, and this lunchtime resilience workshop is here to help you do just that. Through this interactive session, you’ll gain practical strategies and mindset tools to build resilience and take back control of your job search journey. You will learn to: 1. Recognise… thinking patterns that get you down when you need help and where to get it 2. Rewire… your thoughts – experiencing mindfulness for resilience to regulate difficult emotions 3. Ready, Go! Actionable plans to move forward.

Subject: Setting up the Jupyter AI assistant: DSS5102 Advanced Regression and Time Series Analysis [2610]
Preview: - External Email - Dear All, Some of you have been getting an error when setting up the Jupyter AI assistant. If you want to try to get this working, try following the instructions below. Do the following, regardless of whether you're seeing an error or trying to set up for the first time: Download the latest setup_ai_assistant.ipynb from the python-setup folder in our Canvas files. Please download it fresh rather than reusing an older copy, as the notebook has been updated. Open it in JupyterLab and choose Run → Run All Cells . (It's safe to run even if things are currently broken — it repairs the settings.) Fully quit JupyterLab and start it again. A browser refresh is not enough — close the terminal running it, then relaunch with conda activate dss5102 and jupyter lab . Open the Jupyter AI chat (chat icon on the left), then click the settings (gear) icon. If you were seeing an error before, it should be gone and the settings icon should appear. Under Language model, choose Gemini :: gemini-flash-lite-latest . In the API Keys section, paste your key into the GOOGLE_API_KEY field and click Save Changes. If you don't have a key yet, get a free one (no credit card) at https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey — sign in with a Google account and click "Create API key." Ask it a question to test — and remember to always read and understand any code before you use it. One thing to avoid: please don't run pip install jupyter-ai . It's already included in the dss5102 environment, and installing it separately upgrades it to a version that won't work for us. Hope that's helpful for those of you experiencing this problem. Subject: Tutorial week 5 solutions: DSS5102 Advanced Regression and Time Series Analysis [2610]
Preview: - External Email - Hi All, I have uploaded the week 5 tutorial solutions. I have explained a bit in my solutions about two excellent questions raised by students. One is about the issue of "data leakage" in question 1. When doing cross-validation, data leakage occurs when you are using some feature of the test set in prediction that you wouldn't normally know when predicting new data. One way this can occur is through standardization of variables, when that is done using the combined train and test data. I've explained in the notebook why I need to do that here when using the cosine basis. Another question from a student was about the binned residuals in the second question, and how to create the bins using the age variable when a bin might contain only one distinct age value. When ordering by age, there are ties, and the ties are broken by the order of the original observations, with that ordering (in this case) determined by the response variable. This means that you can have bins for a single age value all having the same response, with a zero variance for residuals. I have modified the function for computing binned residuals from class to randomize the order. Needless to say, if you use the function we used in the lectures there is nothing wrong with that too. I am very pleased to see you all engaging with the material in such a thoughtful way. Best, David. View announcement | Update your notification settings

Subject: Track 2: Updated Data Folder (v3) — Inbox Dates, Simulator Options: DSS5105 Data Science Projects in Practice [2610]
Preview: - External Email - Dear Students, Several Track 2 groups sent careful questions about the data folder. They were right on a few points, so here is an updated folder. Your allocator code does not need to change, and normal simulator runs give exactly the same numbers as before. What changed The chat inbox had impossible dates. The inbox is dated 1 April, but many requests asked for orders back in March. That was a mistake in how the file was generated, not a puzzle. Nine requests now point at orders a workshop can actually deliver: R04, R06, R07, R16, R17, R22, R23, R26, R27. The other 21 are unchanged. Three requests (R20, R28, R30) are deliberately impossible — no workshop can make the date — and the right behaviour is to say so with the numbers and offer options, not to allocate silently. The data dictionary now tells you how many requests there are of each kind. "The best ten-line heuristic" was unclear. It means a simple rule-based allocator with no LLM, about the size of the three shipped baselines — for example "earliest estimated finish". The line count does not matter. The simulator's assumptions are now written down : it is a what-if replay of all 120 orders from 1 January; a workshop takes the whole job as one unit of work; one batch goes to one workshop. It is deliberately simple. Also: do not put an LLM call inside your allocator — the simulator should call your deterministic allocation policy, the same tool your chat agent uses. --shock is fixed and now has seeds. Please report --shock results as an average over ten seeds ( python simulate.py --shock --seeds 10 ). The report also shows two extra columns, late days and % def pcs . What "beat the baselines" means is now spelled out per objective in the track description (v4). Optional: for groups who want workshops that can only do some stages, there is an opt-in --stages mode with two extra data files. Ignore it and nothing changes. Which date current_queue_days refers to. A group noticed that this column in workshops.csv is used at two different dates. For the chat inbox , read it as each workshop's queue on 1 April 2026 and use the numbers as they are. The simulator reuses the same numbers as its starting queue on 1 January 2026 , just so every group starts from the same place. Treat the two separately — don't work out one from the other. When a request depends on the queue (for example, "fastest turnaround"), have your system show the numbers it used to decide , and say in your report that you used workshops.csv as the 1 April snapshot . This is only a note in the data dictionary and the simulator header; no numbers change. What you need to re-run If you have already… Do this run your system on the 30 requests Re-run it (9 requests changed) reported --shock numbers Re-run them, averaged over ten seeds reported normal-run numbers Nothing — they are unchanged Updated files Under Week 0 → Capstone Project : Track 1 and Track 2 Data_v3.zip (Track 1's folder is unchanged), Capstone_Project_Spec_v5.pdf and Capstone_Project_Tracks_v4.pdf .
